title: Grammar: Word Formation — Adjectives, Adverbs, and Prefixes
grammarTip:
Прилагательные и наречия для описания экономических концептов:

Изменение/рост:
significantly / considerably / substantially → значительно
slightly / marginally / moderately → незначительно
steadily / consistently → стабильно
dramatically / sharply / rapidly → резко

Тенденции:
to increase/rise/grow → расти (increase in GDP)
to decrease/fall/decline → падать (decline in exports)
to fluctuate → колебаться
to stabilise → стабилизироваться
to peak at → достичь пика
to bottom out → достичь минимума

💡 Для графиков и статистики:
"GDP increased significantly by 5%."
"Unemployment fell sharply from 8% to 3%."
"Exports remained relatively stable."

grammarTable.subject: -al / -ial / -ical
grammarTable.example: economy → economic; globe → global; finance → financial; nation → national; politics → political

grammarTable.subject: -ive / -ative
grammarTable.example: produce → productive; distribute → distributive; compete → competitive; speculate → speculative; inflate → inflationary

grammarTable.subject: -able / -ible
grammarTable.example: sustain → sustainable; access → accessible; afford → affordable; predict → predictable; rely → reliable

grammarTable.subject: -ly
grammarTable.example: significant → significantly; rapid → rapidly; stable → stably; global → globally; general → generally

grammarTable.subject: Negative prefixes
grammarTable.example: equal → unequal; stable → unstable; employed → unemployed; efficient → inefficient; reversible → irreversible

grammarTable.subject: Scale prefixes
grammarTable.example: valued → overvalued/undervalued; priced → overpriced; developed → underdeveloped; economics → macroeconomics/microeconomics

rows.example: "An economic policy is about the economy." / "An economical car uses little fuel." (Note the difference!)
"Financial markets determine interest rates." / "She is financially independent."
"Political decisions shape economic outcomes." / "Politically motivated policies may distort markets."
"Structural unemployment results from changes in the economy's structure." / "Industrial output fell."
"A sustainable economy meets present needs without compromising future ones."
"Affordable housing requires government intervention in most major cities."
"Stable economies are more predictable for businesses planning investments."
"Financial services must be accessible to all citizens, not just the wealthy."

grammarExtra.title: Negative Prefixes: un-, dis-, in-/im-, ir-

rows.example: un-equal, un-employed, un-affordable, un-stable, un-reliable, un-regulated
dis-agree, dis-advantage, dis-invest, dis-trust, dis-proportionate
in-efficient, in-flexible, im-possible, im-perfect, in-adequate, in-accessible

rows.form: ir- = before words beginning with r
rows.example: ir-rational, ir-reversible, ir-regular, ir-responsible

grammarExtra.title: Scale Prefixes: over-, under-, macro-, micro-

rows.example: overvalued (currency worth more than its true value); overproduction; overregulation; overspend
undervalued; underdeveloped; underemployed; underinvestment; underfunded
macroeconomics (study of the whole economy); macroeconomic policy; macro-level analysis
microeconomics (study of individual firms/consumers); microfinance; micro-level decision

grammarExtra.title: Common Economic Word Families with Prefixes

rows.form: employ: employed, unemployed, employer, employee, employment, unemployment, underemployed
rows.example: "High unemployment is a macroeconomic challenge; underemployment is an equally serious microeconomic one."

rows.form: value: valuable, valued, undervalued, overvalued, devalue, evaluate
rows.example: "When a currency is overvalued, exports become uncompetitive and the trade deficit widens."

rows.form: regulate: regulated, unregulated, deregulate, regulator, regulation, over-regulated
rows.example: "An unregulated market may produce externalities that require government intervention."

rows.form: develop: developed, developing, underdeveloped, development, developer, redevelop
rows.example: "In underdeveloped economies, infrastructure investment is a key prerequisite for growth."

exercises.text: "___ markets tend to attract more foreign investment." (stable → adjective with -ble meaning capable of being stable)
exercises.hint: stable → stable (the adjective IS "stable" — no change needed; or: stabilised)

exercises.text: "___ housing is a critical issue in most major cities." (afford → adjective)
exercises.hint: afford → affordable (-able: capable of being afforded)

exercises.text: "The currency was ___ — its value was higher than the true market rate." (over- or under-?)
exercises.hint: over- = too high/more than true value

exercises.text: "Prices rose ___ during the period of hyperinflation." (rapid → adverb)
"High ___ means many people who want to work cannot find a job." (employ → opposite noun)

exercises.instruction: Form the adjective from the verb.
exercises.text: "An ___ market allocates resources better than a planned economy." (compete → adjective: competitive)", (first letter already given)
exercises.hint: compete → competitive (-ive suffix: having the quality of competition)

exercises.text: "___ economics studies individual firms and consumers." (micro- or macro-?)
exercises.hint: micro- = small scale (individuals/firms); macro- = large scale (whole economy)

exercises.text: "Countries with poor infrastructure are often ___ (= less developed than they could be) economically.", (under-)
exercises.hint: under- + developed = underdeveloped (less developed than expected/possible)

exercises.text: "A ___ economy grows in a way that can be maintained long-term." (sustain → adjective)
exercises.hint: sustain → sustainable (-able: capable of being sustained)

exercises.text: "Income is ___ distributed — the top 10% receive most of the gains." (unequal → adverb)", (unequally)
exercises.hint: unequal → unequally (-ly suffix: in an unequal manner)

exercises.text: "Many people are ___ — they have jobs but are working below their skill level." (un + employ)
exercises.hint: under- + employed = underemployed (working below capacity/skill level)

exercises.text: "Some economic models are based on ___ assumptions about human behaviour." (ir + rational)", (irrational)
"The economy grew ___ during the post-war period." (significant → adverb)

exercises.instruction: Form the correct word with a prefix.
exercises.text: "When governments ___ markets, removing rules and restrictions, prices often fall." (re- + regulate → opposite of regulate: deregulate?)", use "deregulate"
"The market was ___ — the regulation was excessive and stifled innovation." (over + regulate + adjective)
"___ economies need infrastructure investment before growth can accelerate.", (under + develop → adjective)
exercises.hint: under- + developed = underdeveloped (less developed than potential)

questions.text: "___ housing requires government intervention in most cities." (afford → adjective)
"High ___ is a major macroeconomic challenge." (employ → negative noun)
"The study of individual firms and consumers is called ___ economics."
"The currency was ___ — its value was lower than its true worth." (under- prefix)
"Income rose ___ during the economic boom." (significant → adverb)
"Economic" (relating to the economy) and "economical" (thrifty/cost-saving) have the same meaning.
questions.hint: "Economic" relates to the economy; "economical" means efficient/cost-saving

questions.text: "A ___ economy grows without depleting future resources." (sustain → adjective)
"Many assumptions in standard economics are ___ — people don't behave rationally." (ir- prefix)
questions.hint: ir- + rational = irrational (before words beginning with r)

questions.text: "Markets need regulation; but ___ (too much regulation) stifles innovation." (over- prefix)
"She is ___ employed — she has a job but it requires far less skill than she has." (under- prefix)
"The government decided to ___ the industry — removing many of the existing regulations." (de- + regulate)
"___ economies with low income levels often face infrastructure shortages." (under- + develop)
